title: Right Under Me
text: Right now my leg is hanging through the ceiling over a hundred dead people, and my best friend is walking right under it.

title: Right Under Me
text: The edge of the hole is cutting into my thigh. My right boot is caught on something sharp. Every time I try to move, a little more white dust falls past my foot.

title: Right Under Me
text: A piece the size of my thumbnail lands on the fountain rim.

title: Right Under Me
text: The little tick carries through the whole court. Under my leg, somebody starts moving.

title: Right Under Me
text: There are faces turned up toward me. A woman with one earring. A man still holding a shopping bag. The cleaner who used to leave a yellow cone outside the bathrooms, even when the floor was dry.

title: Right Under Me
text: And Marcus.

title: Right Under Me
text: He comes around the fountain in his guard uniform, stops at a gate, and shakes it twice.

title: Right Under Me
text: Same as always.

title: Right Under Me
text: The empty clip on his chest catches the emergency light. His radio is in my pocket. I took the battery out before we climbed up here.

title: Right Under Me
text: At least I got one thing right.

title: Right Under Me
text: Above me, Theo is lying flat on a metal beam. He's got both hands around my wrist. His trainers are braced against a pipe, and he's pulling hard enough that his whole face shakes.

title: Right Under Me
text: He looks at my boot.

title: Right Under Me
text: Then he looks at the ceiling around it.

title: Right Under Me
text: “Danny,” he says. “Stop moving.”

title: Right Under Me
text: I stop.

title: Right Under Me
text: Another corner breaks off anyway.

title: Right Under Me
text: The only person who can pull me out is a kid I nearly threw out of my store.

title: Right Under Me
text: Let me back up.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: The woman on the radio asked who was in my daughter's window, and I gave her nothing.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I took my thumb off the button.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: For six years, answering that radio had been my job. A call came in, I said my name, and whoever was on the other end knew somebody was coming.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: Now I had to remind myself that I could leave it alone.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: My phone was in my other hand. No service. My mom's last message was still there, telling me the door was locked. I read it again while the woman waited. I wanted somebody to talk to badly enough that I was afraid of what I might say.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: Across the highway, the tenth-floor window stayed dark. Lily had already blinked three times. I'd answered. Our goodnight was over.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: The woman waited long enough that I could hear her breathing through the little speaker.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “Danny?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I turned the volume down and held the radio against my ear.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “You still there?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I could see a faint light moving behind the department store's rooftop door. When I looked again, it was gone.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I pressed the button.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “How did you get inside?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: A little laugh.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “That's a fairly rude first question.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “You asked me one.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “Fair enough. Vera. There. Now you have a name.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I waited.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “I was trying on a coat. Department store. Second floor. Sat down in the fitting room and fell asleep. By the time I woke up, they'd locked the place.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: The store had closed at nine. At midnight, I'd checked the staff corridor behind those fitting rooms. I'd heard nothing.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “What coat?” I asked.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “What?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “The one you were trying on.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “Danny, there are people eating people downstairs. I think we've moved beyond the returns policy.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: She sounded almost amused.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: Then her voice changed a little.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “There's a girl up here with me. She's hungry. Have you got anything we could eat?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I looked at Lily's window again. Kept my thumb away from the button while I did it.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “How old?”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: “Little. Six, perhaps. Seven. It's hard to get much out of her.”

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: I stood on that roof until my hand went numb around the radio.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: Vera never asked about the window again that night.

title: The Woman in the Fitting Room
text: She'd found another question I couldn't walk away from.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Somebody ate my breakfast while I slept inside a locked store.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I'd put two protein bars beside the tent. One for when I woke up, one for later, because apparently I needed a system for deciding when to eat cardboard.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: There was one left.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I checked the sleeping bag. Turned it inside out. Looked under the tent and inside both boots.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: At the gate, the padlock was closed. Key thirty-one was still on my belt.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I counted the water twice.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: A bottle was missing too.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I could explain losing a protein bar. I'd spent the night listening to my dead friend walk past, and my brain was doing its best to forget the whole thing.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: A bottle was harder.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I lined everything up along the back wall. Bars in one row, cans in another, water underneath. Wrote the numbers on a receipt with the little pencil I used for my shift log.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I hadn't written anything in that log since the first night.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: For a while I sat there trying to remember the last normal entry. A door propped open. A car parked across two spaces. Something I'd been annoyed about.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Then I heard two pulls on a gate outside, and I remembered I was supposed to be counting water.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I carried the remaining bars into the stockroom and put them in a plastic storage box. Then I sat beside it until my neck hurt.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Nothing happened.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: At nine, I went to the roof. Three blinks from Lily. Three back from me. I kept my body between the flashlight and the department store.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Vera called as soon as I came downstairs.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: “Any luck with supper?”

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: “I haven't agreed to anything.”

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: “You sound tired.”

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: “I am tired.”

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: “Get some rest. We can talk tomorrow.”

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: I stared at the storage box for another hour.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: When I finally slept, I put it beside my head.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: When I woke again, the lid was back on. One of the catches hadn't quite clicked shut.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Two more bars were gone.

title: Breakfast for Somebody Else
text: Whoever was doing this had stood close enough to watch me sleep.

title: The Footprints
text: I put climbing chalk on the floor, and the footprints went up the wall.

title: The Footprints
text: The chalk came in a little white bag from the climbing display. I spread it around the food box, under the stockroom door, and across the narrow space between the tents.

title: The Footprints
text: Then I went back to bed with my boots on.

title: The Footprints
text: That was my entire investigation. Six years in security, and I was waiting for somebody to step in powder.

title: The Footprints
text: I left a fresh bar on top of the box. The rest went inside it.

title: The Footprints
text: I felt ridiculous setting bait with a breakfast I couldn't afford to lose. But the gate was the only way in that I understood. Whoever had found another way could bring somebody else through it.

title: The Footprints
text: I lay facing the gap between the tents. If anybody came through there, this time I'd see them.

title: The Footprints
text: Sometime before morning, I heard plastic bend.

title: The Footprints
text: By the time I'd got out of the sleeping bag, the store was still again.

title: The Footprints
text: I left the overhead lights off and used my flashlight close to the floor.

title: The Footprints
text: Small trainers. A worn patch under the right heel. The print had a little square of clear floor in the middle where the sole was split.

title: The Footprints
text: The trail came from behind the climbing wall display.

title: The Footprints
text: It went to the food box.

title: The Footprints
text: Then it went back.

title: The Footprints
text: I moved the display a few inches. Behind it was a tall storage rack bolted to the wall. A shoeprint showed on the bottom shelf. Another was pressed against the painted wall halfway up.

title: The Footprints
text: Higher still, somebody had wiped a hand across a dusty pipe.

title: The Footprints
text: I followed the pipe with the light.

title: The Footprints
text: One ceiling tile was cleaner around the edges than all the others.

title: The Footprints
text: I stood there with my mouth open.

title: The Footprints
text: Every door was locked. Every window was intact. I'd checked the gates so often that morning my hand hurt.

title: The Footprints
text: I hadn't looked up once.

title: The Footprints
text: A little white flake dropped out of the seam above me.

title: The Footprints
text: I switched the flashlight off.

title: The Footprints
text: Whoever was up there had seen the light.

title: The Footprints
text: And they were still there.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I caught the person stealing my food, and he was wearing shoes held together with tape.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I waited behind the display until my bad knee went stiff. It was barely six in the morning. Outside, Marcus rattled the gate and moved on.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: The tile lifted.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: Two fingers appeared, then a head, then a very skinny boy lowering himself onto the top shelf.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He moved carefully. He knew which bit of the rack squeaked. He stepped around it before his foot even touched down.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: When he reached the floor, he went straight to the box. I waited until he bent over it. Then I stood up.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: We looked at each other.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He had a protein bar already in his hand.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: The sweatshirt hung past his fingers. There was a pale clean line around one wrist where he'd pushed a sleeve up. Everything else about him looked as dusty as the pipe.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I'd practised this conversation in my head while I waited. It had involved a grown man explaining himself.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I hadn't practised what to do if the thief looked hungry enough to eat the wrapper.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Put it down,” I said.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He put it down.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: Then he ran straight at me.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I moved aside because, for a second, that's what my body thought you did when a kid ran at you. He got past, took two steps up the rack, and nearly reached the pipe.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I caught the back of his sweatshirt.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He twisted so hard the stitching tore.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Let go.”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Stop kicking.”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Let go.”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I did.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He stayed on the second shelf, one hand on the pipe, watching my hands.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: The loose shelf knocked against the wall.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: Somewhere outside, a shoe dragged across the floor.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: We both stopped breathing.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: A shadow passed the gate. Paused. Moved on.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: The boy looked toward the hallway, then back at me.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Don't do that again,” he whispered.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: I wanted to tell him I was the adult and this was my store and he was stealing my food.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: Instead I asked how old he was.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Fifteen.”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Your name?”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Theo.”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Who else is up there?”

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: He tightened his grip on the pipe.

title: A Pair of Trainers
text: “Nobody. That's why I stay up there.”

title: Four Months
text: A fifteen-year-old had been living in my mall for four months, and I'd never noticed.

title: Four Months
text: I let him sit on an overturned camping bucket. He kept the rack within reach.

title: Four Months
text: “Where do you sleep?”

title: Four Months
text: “Above the cinema.”

title: Four Months
text: “In the ceiling?”

title: Four Months
text: “There's a space beside the projection room.”

title: Four Months
text: “For four months?”

title: Four Months
text: He shrugged. A tiny movement. Like he was trying to make four months smaller.

title: Four Months
text: “How did you eat?”

title: Four Months
text: “People throw stuff out.”

title: Four Months
text: “And the doors?”

title: Four Months
text: “I go round them.”

title: Four Months
text: I looked up at the tile again.

title: Four Months
text: He pointed toward my belt.

title: Four Months
text: “You like checking those.”

title: Four Months
text: “The keys?”

title: Four Months
text: “The doors. You do the same ones twice when you're on the phone.”

title: Four Months
text: I thought about all the nights I'd walked this building, tugged handles, signed the log, and told myself everybody was safe.

title: Four Months
text: Theo peeled a strip of tape away from his trainer. Pressed it back down.

title: Four Months
text: “You sing in the freight elevator,” he said.

title: Four Months
text: I looked at him.

title: Four Months
text: “Usually the same song. You only know some of it.”

title: Four Months
text: My face got hot. Even then. Even with everything outside, that still worked.

title: Four Months
text: “You can't stay here,” I said.

title: Four Months
text: The words came out before I'd decided what I meant by them.

title: Four Months
text: There were two sentences in my head. One was about food. The other was about the man who'd sat outside my gate and trusted me to know what to do.

title: Four Months
text: I could hardly look at that gate in daylight. Now this kid was sitting six feet from it, waiting for me to be in charge.

title: Four Months
text: I wanted somebody qualified. A firefighter. His dad. Any adult who'd know how to keep him alive.

title: Four Months
text: He was looking at the only one available.

title: Four Months
text: Theo stood immediately.

title: Four Months
text: He didn't argue. Picked up nothing, because he'd brought nothing.

title: Four Months
text: I heard Marcus at another gate down the hall.

title: Four Months
text: Theo heard him too.

title: Four Months
text: “Wait,” I said.

title: Four Months
text: He waited beside the rack.

title: Four Months
text: I reached for a bottle, then stopped with my hand on it.

title: Four Months
text: Theo watched me count the ones left.

title: Four Months
text: “How long have you got?” he asked.

title: Four Months
text: “About ten days. Maybe. I was working it out for one person.”

title: Four Months
text: He looked toward the front of the mall.

title: Four Months
text: “I know where there's eight thousand gallons.”

title: The Fountain
text: The water I needed was under a hundred dead people.

title: The Fountain
text: “The fountain,” Theo said.

title: The Fountain
text: I stared at him.

title: The Fountain
text: In six years I'd taken coins out of that fountain, fished out a phone, and once helped a man retrieve an engagement ring he'd dropped before he got to the important question.

title: The Fountain
text: I'd never thought about where the water came from.

title: The Fountain
text: “Big tank underneath,” Theo said. “There's a room with all the pumps. Number's written on the side.”

title: The Fountain
text: “Eight thousand?”

title: The Fountain
text: He nodded.

title: The Fountain
text: I knew the pump-room door. It opened into the center court, beside the pretzel place. On the cameras, that doorway was buried behind bodies.

title: The Fountain
text: “The way downstairs is full.”

title: The Fountain
text: “I come from above.”

title: The Fountain
text: He drew a route in the chalk with one finger. Above the cinema. Across a service walkway. Down inside the big column beside the fountain, on a maintenance ladder.

title: The Fountain
text: The route ended behind the locked pump-room door.

title: The Fountain
text: I could feel the weight of the keys on my hip.

title: The Fountain
text: “Why haven't you gone already?”

title: The Fountain
text: “Nothing to carry it in.”

title: The Fountain
text: The store around us was full of camping water containers.

title: The Fountain
text: “How much can you carry back?” I asked.

title: The Fountain
text: He held his hands a little apart.

title: The Fountain
text: “Small ones. You have to get them through.”

title: The Fountain
text: I picked up a container big enough to be useful, imagined carrying it one-handed over the court, and put it back.

title: The Fountain
text: We settled on two smaller ones. I tried holding them full, then lifting them onto a shelf. My arms shook by the third try.

title: The Fountain
text: Theo watched without saying anything. I wished he'd made a joke. It would've been easier than watching him decide whether I could do it.

title: The Fountain
text: He looked at them. Looked at me.

title: The Fountain
text: We understood each other then.

title: The Fountain
text: I'd been counting bottles and locking gates. He'd been counting routes through walls.

title: The Fountain
text: That night Vera called again. She said the little girl had stopped asking for food.

title: The Fountain
text: I held the radio so tightly the plastic creaked.

title: The Fountain
text: “Get some sleep, Danny,” she said. “You'll think better tomorrow.”

title: The Fountain
text: I sat beside Theo's bucket after the light went out.

title: The Fountain
text: “Show me the way,” I said. “We bring water back. You get food. We work the rest out after.”

title: The Fountain
text: He looked at the tent, then at the rack.

title: The Fountain
text: I'd come down from the roof a few minutes earlier. Lily had blinked. I'd blinked back. For another night, that was everything we knew about each other.

title: The Fountain
text: My mom had gone into the apartment with about ten days of insulin. Every time I counted my water, I found myself counting her days too.

title: The Fountain
text: Getting more water wouldn't get me across the highway. But I couldn't do anything for either of them if I spent the next week getting too weak to climb the roof ladder.

title: The Fountain
text: “You coming too?”

title: The Fountain
text: “Yes.”

title: The Fountain
text: He glanced at my boots.

title: The Fountain
text: That was when I started worrying about what his route could hold.

title: Key Seventeen
text: The first new door I opened was beside a kid's bed.

title: Key Seventeen
text: We left before the mall got bright. I took empty camping containers, a flashlight, and a strap from the climbing display.

title: Key Seventeen
text: I took the battery out of Marcus's radio. Wrapped the keyring in a sock so the metal would stay quiet.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Theo made me try the rack without the containers first. On the second shelf I reached for something that looked solid. He caught my hand before I put any weight on it.

title: Key Seventeen
text: “That's for holding the ceiling up,” he said. “It won't hold you.”

title: Key Seventeen
text: He moved my hand to a thick support above it.

title: Key Seventeen
text: I nodded as if I'd understood that all along. Then I climbed down and started again.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Theo watched all of it.

title: Key Seventeen
text: “You always carry that many?”

title: Key Seventeen
text: “Every night.”

title: Key Seventeen
text: “Must've been annoying.”

title: Key Seventeen
text: It had been. I would've given almost anything to be annoyed by that sound again on an ordinary Tuesday.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Above the store, the air was warm and smelled like dust from a heater somebody had just switched on. Theo showed me where the metal supports ran.

title: Key Seventeen
text: I followed them on my hands and knees. Kept my weight on the heavy steel. The ceiling tiles shifted below us when I breathed too hard.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Over the cinema, he stopped beside a stained blanket.

title: Key Seventeen
text: There were three empty water bottles, a folded hoodie, and a photograph turned face down. He slid that underneath the blanket before I could see it.

title: Key Seventeen
text: A door beside the little platform had CINEMA SERVICE stencilled across it.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Key seventeen fit.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Theo watched the lock turn as though I'd done a trick.

title: Key Seventeen
text: “You've been climbing around this?”

title: Key Seventeen
text: “For a while.”

title: Key Seventeen
text: I opened it just wide enough for us to get through.

title: Key Seventeen
text: On the other side was the service walkway over the center court. Through gaps beneath the rail, I could see the tops of heads.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Theo stepped out first.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Halfway across, the proper walkway ended. Beyond it, the route followed a pair of supports above the suspended ceiling.

title: Key Seventeen
text: I stopped.

title: Key Seventeen
text: Theo looked back.

title: Key Seventeen
text: “Don't put your foot where you think the floor is.”

title: The Rattle Below
text: My best friend walked his rounds while I crawled over his head.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Theo crossed the first gap easily. I watched where his hands went, then tried to put mine in the same places.

title: The Rattle Below
text: There was a difference between watching a skinny fifteen-year-old do something and asking my knees to do it afterward.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Sweat ran down my nose. I caught it on my sleeve before it could fall.

title: The Rattle Below
text: One of the emergency lights flickered underneath us. For a second the shadows moved and I tightened both hands on the steel.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Theo stopped with me. He didn't tell me to hurry.

title: The Rattle Below
text: “Next hand,” he whispered.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I moved it.

title: The Rattle Below
text: “Now your knee.”

title: The Rattle Below
text: I moved that too.

title: The Rattle Below
text: After a while I could do two movements without being told. I was grateful he didn't mention it.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Below us, the fountain was dark. Coins lay on the bottom. The people around it were standing shoulder to shoulder in places, their faces turned toward the food-court doors.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I stopped counting at a hundred.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Theo reached back for a container. I passed it forward. He put it on a solid section, then came back for the other one.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Slow. Everything had to be slow.

title: The Rattle Below
text: A gate rattled at the far end of the hall.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I knew who it was before I saw him.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Marcus came around the corner and stopped at the first store. Two pulls on the gate. A pause. Then the next one.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I found myself waiting for him to look up.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Theo touched my shoulder.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I moved my knee to give him room.

title: The Rattle Below
text: The bit of metal under it folded.

title: The Rattle Below
text: I dropped far enough that my stomach hit the edge of the support. My right leg punched through a tile. Something caught the leather of my boot and held it there.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Pieces fell into the court.

title: The Rattle Below
text: The first one struck the fountain's rim.

title: The Rattle Below
text: A head turned.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Then another.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Theo caught my wrist. I tried to pull my knee back, and a sharp edge dug into my thigh.

title: The Rattle Below
text: Below, Marcus stopped walking.

title: The Rattle Below
text: He lifted his face toward my foot.

title: The Rattle Below
text: My boot began to slide off.

title: Hold On
text: The kid I'd told to leave was the only thing keeping me out of that crowd.

title: Hold On
text: Theo lay flat and reached for my other wrist. His fingers slipped on my sleeve.

title: Hold On
text: “Give me your hand.”

title: Hold On
text: I tried.

title: Hold On
text: A long piece of the tile broke away and hit someone's shoulder. People began pushing under the hole. Slowly, one body leaning into the next.

title: Hold On
text: Marcus stood among them, looking up.

title: Hold On
text: I could see the worn patch on his cap. I'd stood beside him in the office while he picked at it with his thumbnail and told me a joke I'd already heard.

title: Hold On
text: I nearly said his name.

title: Hold On
text: Theo hit my arm.

title: Hold On
text: “Look at me.”

title: Hold On
text: I looked up.

title: Hold On
text: He was reaching for the strap I'd brought. Getting it around the heavy support with one hand while the other held my sleeve.

title: Hold On
text: “You have to let go,” he whispered.

title: Hold On
text: I shook my head.

title: Hold On
text: “One hand. I need the strap.”

title: Hold On
text: His sleeve was bunched in my fist. I'd been holding him so hard the cloth had twisted around his arm.

title: Hold On
text: I made myself open my fingers.

title: Hold On
text: He fed the strap around the support and leaned his weight into it. I heard fabric pull tight. His shoe slipped against the brace, and he caught himself with a sharp little breath.

title: Hold On
text: Then his hand was back in front of my face.

title: Hold On
text: “Elbow up,” he said. “You have to help.”

title: Hold On
text: I got an elbow onto the steel. Pushed until my shoulder felt as though it was coming apart. Theo leaned back against the strap and pulled.

title: Hold On
text: My boot stayed where it was.

title: Hold On
text: My foot came out of it.

title: Hold On
text: For a second I thought that meant I was falling.

title: Hold On
text: Then my knee slid over the edge, and Theo dragged me onto the solid platform with him.

title: Hold On
text: We lay there together, breathing into our sleeves.

title: Hold On
text: Below us, the boot finally came loose.

title: Hold On
text: It landed inside the empty fountain with a noise that seemed to go on forever.

title: Hold On
text: Theo pressed both palms against the metal and waited.

title: Hold On
text: Eventually the pushing slowed. A few faces turned away.

title: Hold On
text: I looked at him.

title: Hold On
text: His trouser leg was torn at the calf. There was blood on the sharp brace he'd crawled across to reach me.

title: Hold On
text: He pulled the fabric down over it.

title: Hold On
text: “You can walk without that shoe,” he whispered.

title: Hold On
text: Somewhere ahead and below us, water dripped.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: We found enough water to keep the whole mall alive, and Theo told me what had brought the dead there.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: The maintenance ladder ran down inside the service column. At the bottom, a narrow hatch opened into the pump room beneath the fountain.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: I put my good foot on each rung first. Theo stayed close enough to hear every breath I was trying to keep quiet.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: The tank took up most of the room.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: EIGHT THOUSAND GALLONS was printed on a plate beside its inspection window.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: There was water behind the glass.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: I put my hand against the tank and left it there for a while.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: We still had to get it back and treat it with the gear in the store. But I could stop staring at the last few bottles every time I swallowed.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: Theo eased himself onto the bottom rung. He was favouring his leg.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “You hurt?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “Caught it.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “I saw.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “Then why'd you ask?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: I nearly smiled.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: We filled what we could carry.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: The handles pulled at my fingers when I lifted the containers. We'd be drinking what we carried back for days. After that, we'd have to come again. The thought of that crossing again made me put one down.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: Theo noticed.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “We can find a better bit to cross,” he said.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “You know one?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “I can look.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: I held the handle again. He'd spent four months figuring this place out because he had to. I was going to have to start doing the same.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: Outside the pump-room door, a shoe scraped along the floor. Dust shook out of the frame.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: Theo stared at that door.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “This is where they were,” he said.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “Who?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “The drill people.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: I set the container down.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “Three of them. A woman and two men. Behind the pretzel place. First night.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “What time?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “One-thirty. I could see the clock through the opening.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: One-thirty. Ten minutes before Marcus called about the man on the ramp.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “They were cutting through the wall,” Theo said. “Loud as a chainsaw. I could hear it all the way at the cinema.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: He rubbed his sleeve over his nose.

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “People started coming in. Through the service hall. They just kept coming.”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “What did the woman do?”

title: Eight Thousand Gallons
text: “Told them to keep drilling.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: The dead had followed a drill into my mall, and my best friend had been in their way.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I sat on the bottom rung beside Theo.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: Through the door, I could hear somebody's hand dragging over the wall.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “The woman on my radio?” I asked.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “Same voice. I heard her in your store last night.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “You're sure?”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “She was right below me when they were drilling, Danny.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I looked at the door.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “They saw them?”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: Theo nodded.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “One of the men went to look. Came back running. The woman kept saying another minute.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “And then?”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “They took the machine and went through the staff door. I stayed where I was until it got quiet.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: The food court. The broken glass. The service halls filling up.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I'd watched all those cameras and thought the crowd was wandering through any door it found.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I'd been watching where they went. Theo had heard what they were following.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “Was there a kid with them?”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: Theo shook his head.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “A little girl?”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “No.”

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I heard Vera's voice again. Soft through the speaker. The little girl had stopped asking for food.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I stood up too fast and hit my shoulder on the ladder.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: Theo caught the container before it struck the floor.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: For a moment I wanted to go straight to the department store. Stand outside her gate and make her tell me why she'd kept that drill going.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: My keys were still wrapped in the sock.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I closed my hand around them until the teeth pressed through the fabric.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: “Danny,” Theo said.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I looked at his leg. At the blood drying on the edge of his trainer.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: He had followed me down here. Now he was waiting for me to get him back.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I picked up the water.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: On the return trip, we moved around the broken section. It took nearly an hour. I could see my boot in the fountain below.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I could see Marcus too.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: At the cinema, Theo stopped to pick up his blanket. He tucked the photograph inside it. I pretended to be busy with the containers.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I got back to Summit Outdoors in one boot and a filthy sock. Theo went down first and cleared a place for the containers. Then he steadied the rack while I climbed.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I reached the floor and put my hand on the padlock.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: Closed. Exactly where I'd left it.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I let go and turned toward Theo. He was sitting on the bucket, trying to bend his trouser leg far enough to see the cut.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I'd checked that lock so many times. Theo had just brought me home without going anywhere near it.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: I got the first-aid box.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: At nine, I climbed to the roof alone. Three lights from Lily. Three back. I held the roof hatch open a little on the way down, so I could see whether Theo was still there.

title: Somebody Called Them
text: He was asleep beside the water.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I told the boy who'd saved me to pick a tent, and he asked what it would cost.

title: Pick a Tent
text: We'd got back the afternoon before. I'd used bottled water to clean the scrape on his leg and found a bandage in the first-aid display.

title: Pick a Tent
text: He'd let me do it without looking at me once.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I'd asked him to tell me if it got worse. He'd said he would, much too quickly.

title: Pick a Tent
text: Later, I'd found him putting the empty wrapper from his bandage inside another wrapper, folding both down until they took up almost no room. He'd done the same with his food.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I knew that habit. I'd seen it in the places above the cinema. A whole life packed small enough that you could move it before somebody told you to.

title: Pick a Tent
text: That morning he was beside the rack with his blanket rolled under one arm.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Where are you going?”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Back.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Your leg's hurting.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “It's fine.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: He shifted his weight onto the other foot.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I looked at the ceiling tile. His way out was three shelves up, above the pipe he'd used while I slept.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Pick a tent,” I said.

title: Pick a Tent
text: He watched me.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Any of them. Except that one. I'm in that one.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “For how long?”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “We'll work it out.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “What do you want?”

title: Pick a Tent
text: That question made me put down the box I was holding.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Help with the water. Keep things quiet. Tell me if you hear people up there.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: He waited.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “That's it,” I said.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I got him a clean sweatshirt from a shelf. He folded it so carefully before he put it down that I had to find something else to look at.

title: Pick a Tent
text: Vera called near dusk.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Danny. Any room at the inn?”

title: Pick a Tent
text: I held the radio close to my ear.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Still there?” she asked.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I pressed the button.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “You said you were trying on a coat.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Yes.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Before the mall closed.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Eventually you're going to have to explain this interest in my shopping.”

title: Pick a Tent
text: Theo was watching me from the open tent.

title: Pick a Tent
text: I let go of the button. Left her waiting this time.

title: Pick a Tent
text: At five to nine, I took the flashlight from the shelf.

title: Pick a Tent
text: Theo pulled on the clean sweatshirt.

title: Pick a Tent
text: “Can I see?” he asked.

title: Somebody Answered
text: A stranger blinked my daughter's goodnight signal from the department store roof.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Before that happened, I let Theo come up with me.

title: Somebody Answered
text: He stood a little behind the hatch, keeping his weight off the bandaged leg. Across the highway, Parkview was barely visible against the sky.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I found the tenth floor. Counted to the fourth window from the left.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I always counted. Even when I already knew where to look.

title: Somebody Answered
text: At nine, the flashlight came on.

title: Somebody Answered
text: One. Two. Three.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I answered with my own.

title: Somebody Answered
text: My hands were steadier than they'd been the night before. I had water downstairs. There was another person waiting beside me, alive, who could hear something fall and help me pick it up.

title: Somebody Answered
text: It took so little to make me feel better that I almost missed the light to my right.

title: Somebody Answered
text: It came from the department store roof.

title: Somebody Answered
text: One.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Two.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Three.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Pointed across the highway.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Toward her window.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I lowered my flashlight.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I wanted to blink again. Correct it somehow. Tell Lily which light was mine.

title: Somebody Answered
text: But we had three flashes, and we had the emergency signal. That was all. I'd never taught her what to do when somebody else answered.

title: Somebody Answered
text: My thumb rested on the switch while the department store roof went dark.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I kept it there until I was sure I wouldn't press it.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Theo looked from that roof to me.

title: Somebody Answered
text: “Who is that?” he asked.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I put the light in my pocket before I answered.

title: Somebody Answered
text: “The woman.”

title: Somebody Answered
text: The radio stayed off.

title: Somebody Answered
text: In front of us, Lily's window went dark. Our goodnight was over. Somebody else had joined it.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I stood there until Theo touched my sleeve.

title: Somebody Answered
text: He was looking at the keys. The sock had come loose when I'd put the flashlight away. The last red tag hung against my hand.

title: Somebody Answered
text: “What's B3?” he asked.

title: Somebody Answered
text: I looked down.

title: Somebody Answered
text: “Why?”

title: Somebody Answered
text: “That woman. She kept saying it. Down to B3. Get to the door.”

title: Somebody Answered
text: I closed my fingers around the tag.

title: Somebody Answered
text: “They weren't trying to get into a shop,” he said. “They were trying to get underneath it.”

title: Somebody Answered
text: I thought of Walt tapping the last key. Don't ask.

title: Somebody Answered
text: Across the highway was my daughter. Across the roof was a woman copying her signal.

title: Somebody Answered
text: And the thing that woman wanted was hanging from my belt.

title: Somebody Answered
text: What did she think was behind that door?
